title: Vertical Federated K-Means for Multi-View Data Guided by a K-Means Cost Bound after Projection

problem.claim: Multi-view clustering must address distributed storage of different views, data protection needs, privacy-preserving clustering consistency, and feature-space differences that hinder cross-view information sharing and fusion.

gap.claim: Vertical federated clustering lacks a theoretical analysis of clustering consistency between client-uploaded data and original client data, and faces difficulty sharing and fusing information across different client feature spaces.

contributions.claim: The paper provides an upper-bound analysis of k-means loss under transformation-matrix mapping, relating transformed-data loss to original-data loss.

The paper proposes V-HDKM, a vertical federated clustering method that transposes client feature matrices, expands the feature space, clusters feature centers, and iteratively aggregates centers for cross-view fusion.
The paper reports that implementation code is available at the supplied GitHub URL.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that V-HDKM significantly improves local clustering performance and performs better than seven other vertical federated methods on 20 multi-view datasets.
The authors report stability with respect to the number of clients in sensitivity analysis on 8 UCI datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-view data is common, and multi-view clustering is used to capture its grouping structure.
Real-world requirements motivate vertical federated clustering, which faces privacy-related consistency analysis and cross-client feature-space fusion challenges.
The approach derives a projected k-means loss bound and proposes V-HDKM, using feature-matrix transposition, feature-space expansion, center aggregation, and iterative feedback.
The authors report comparative performance on 20 multi-view datasets and stability analysis on 8 UCI datasets.
Code availability is reported through a GitHub repository.

source_observation.claim: The method uses a theoretical projected k-means loss bound to guide feature-space expansion and center-based iterative fusion across clients.

interpretation.claim: A loss bound can serve as a design guide for privacy-preserving distributed representation and aggregation.

application.claim: In other vertically partitioned learning settings, derive bounds for transformed or uploaded representations before designing aggregation procedures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported clustering setting or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the form or assumptions of the k-means loss upper bound.
The abstract does not describe the privacy mechanism or quantify privacy guarantees.
The abstract does not provide dataset identities, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported experiments.
